title: Genoa's Motorway Viaduct Got 23,000 Euros a Year. Then It Came Down.
title_candidates: Genoa's Motorway Viaduct Got 23,000 Euros a Year. Then It Came Down.
Thirty-Two Were Convicted at First Instance in Genoa. The Judgment Is Not Final.
description:
At eleven thirty-six in the morning, on the fourteenth of August 2018, the balanced system at pier nine of the Polcevera viaduct in Genoa, and the two infill decks joining it to the spans on either side, came down. About two hundred and forty-three metres of road. Forty-three people were killed. Thirteen were injured. Those are the figures in the ministry's own report.

On the cause, the record holds two findings, and they do not agree. The ministry's own commission, appointed the day of the collapse and reporting a month later, held it more likely that the first cause was not the rupture of one or more stays but the failure of one of the remaining structural elements — the edge beams of the infill decks, or the box-girder decks — conditioned by the advanced state of corrosion, and it called its own account plausible but not definitive. Two years later a panel of experts appointed by the investigating judge identified, as reported at the time, corrosion in the upper part of the south stay, on the Genoa side, of pier nine. We have not read that report, and this film does not choose between the two findings.

This film is about the paper. The company that held the road under a concession signed in October 2007 checked its structures by inspection: somebody looked, and wrote a score out of a hundred in a box, against a manual the company itself had written. In that manual, reduction of the prestressing steel section — broken wires — is a seventy, and for a seventy immediate measures are provided, up to closure of the carriageway. On 1 August 2012 an inspection under this viaduct recorded concrete detached, cables in view and some of the wires broken. The number written in the box was forty.

What the record also holds: structural works on the whole viaduct from 1982 to 2018 totalled 24,610,500 euros, and 98 per cent of that was spent before 1999 — the year the motorway company was privatised. In the seventeen years to 1999, structural work on the viaduct averaged one point three million euros a year. In the nineteen years after, about 23,000. Under a 2003 order, a formal safety assessment of the viaduct was owed by March 2013. On 23 June 2017 the company stated in a numbered letter to the ministry that it had been carried out. The commission found that it had not — that no safety analysis and no seismic assessment of the viaduct was ever made. From 28 March 2013 to 24 October 2017 the observations box of the inspection sheets carries no further comments, and the text annotated in previous years is deleted. And the commission wrote that the concessionaire did not make use of the powers the highway code conferred on it to restrict or prohibit traffic on the viaduct.

SOURCES
- Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti, Commissione Ispettiva Ministeriale, report on the collapse of the Polcevera viaduct, Rome, 14 September 2018
- Tribunale di Genova, operative part of the first-instance judgment, 16 July 2026 — read in full
- The company's own inspection manual, as quoted inside the commission's report
- The court-appointed experts' report of December 2020 — as reported at the time; we have not read it
- Named-outlet reporting of the trial and the verdict

Every factual line in the narration is sourced to one of those. Where the record does not carry something — what was in the report the company asked Morandi for in 1981, the reasoning behind the judgment, which element failed first — the film says so out loud instead of filling the gap.

ON THE JUDGMENT, AS OF AUGUST 2026
The trial opened in Genoa in July 2022, with 57 defendants. On 16 July 2026 the court read out its decision: 32 people were convicted, and 25 were acquitted or their charges declared time-barred. The former chief executive of the motorway company, Giovanni Castellucci, was convicted at first instance and sentenced to twelve years; his lawyers said they would appeal, and the judgment is not final. The convictions are for negligence. For every one of those defendants the court struck out the aggravating circumstance of having acted while foreseeing the event, and every defendant charged with the two intentional offences was acquitted. The court gave itself ninety days to write down its reasons. When this film was made, those reasons had not been filed, and this is a first-instance judgment in a country with three instances.

ABOUT THE IMAGES
This film uses AI-assisted visualizations. They are symbolic reconstructions, not photographs of the event, and they contain no likeness of any real person. The fall itself is never depicted. No victim is named, shown or described anywhere in this film.
